title: Spark Delegates are identified confidentially to the Foundation while remaining anonymous to the public
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.4.2.1 requires every prospective Delegate to "complete an initial, confidential identity verification process with the Spark Foundation, subject to additional KYC verification as necessary in the future," then states plainly: "Delegates may remain anonymous or pseudonymous to the public."

Accountability is thus split by audience. To the Foundation, a Delegate is a legally identified person subject to sanctions screening (.4.2.3), conflict-of-interest filing (.4.2.2), an ongoing duty to report material legal changes on pain of automatic suspension (.4.2.4), and immediate removal for refusing updated KYC (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.5.3). To SPK holders, a Delegate may be nothing but a pseudonym and a voting record.

The justification is that public identification would deter capable delegates: governance participants attract legal exposure, harassment and coercion, and demanding public identity selects for those who can afford that exposure rather than those who vote well.

The cost is that token holders cannot assess the conflicts themselves. A delegator choosing where to send their voting power cannot see whether a delegate is employed by a counterparty of Spark, because the disclosure went to the Foundation privately. Holders must trust the Foundation's screening rather than verify it — which concentrates yet another dependency in the same entity that appoints, pays and renews the delegate.
description: Identity verification, conflict disclosure and sanctions screening run privately through the Spark Foundation, and Delegates may stay pseudonymous to token holders.
